summary: The study demonstrates the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to deposit Hf-aluminate films with controlled composition to suppress crystallization in Hf-based gate dielectrics. The films are composed of HfO2 and Al2O3, with the Hf fraction ranging from 20% to 100%. The process uses H2O/HfCl4 and H2O/TMA as precursors, and the films are deposited at 300 °C. The thermal stability of the amorphous phase is significantly improved by alloying HfO2 with Al2O3, with films containing up to 75% Al remaining amorphous after a 1050 °C spike anneal.
evidence: We demonstrate significantly improved thermal stability of the amorphous phase for hafnium-based gate dielectrics through the controlled addition of Al2O3 using atomic layer deposition. The (HfO2)x(Al2O3)12x films, deposited using atomic layer deposition, exhibit excellent control over a wide range of composition by a suitable choice of the ratio between the Al and Hf precursor pulses. The two pairs of precursors pulsed in each deposition cycle were H2O/HfCl4 (hafnium tetrachloride) and H2O/TMA (trimethylaluminum), for depositing HfO2 and Al2O3, respectively. The films were deposited in an ASM Pulsar2000™ module at a substrate temperature of 300 °C.
